cur:manuscripts-paris-gregory-good-samar.summary: The top register shows the prophet Nathan rebuking the kneeling King David; the middle tells the parable of the man who fell among thieves on the road from Jerusalem to Jericho, with the haloed Christ, wearing a cross-nimbus, coming to his aid; in the lowest register Christ, followed by his disciples, approaches a bier where a dead woman lies surrounded by mourners. The page sets repentance and Christ's mercy side by side.
facts: Many of its full-page miniatures do not illustrate Gregory's sermons directly but set biblical and historical scenes beside them as a commentary devised for the court.
Captions in Greek name the places Jerusalem and Jericho in the parable scene.
cur:manuscripts-paris-gregory-good-samar.notes: Folio derived from the Gallica image sequence (view number minus 13, halved) and checked against folios named on other Commons files of this manuscript; the Commons file name gives the Gallica view number, not the folio. The identification of the lowest scene (a raising of the dead) is tentative because of paint loss.

cur:manuscripts-trier-apocalypse-pergamo.summary: From a band of sky at the top left, the bust of Christ with a cross-staff looks down; below, John points toward a group of men, while at the bottom another figure gestures toward a woman lying on an ornate bed beside lamps. The scene illustrates the warnings in the letters to the churches.
facts: The Trier Apocalypse contains 74 full-page drawings illustrating about 150 episodes of the Book of Revelation; it is one of the earliest illustrated Apocalypse manuscripts to survive.
Its pictures are thought to copy a late antique model of the 4th–6th century, which explains features such as books shown as scrolls and Christ as the beardless Logos.
cur:manuscripts-trier-apocalypse-pergamo.notes: The lower scene (a woman on a bed) corresponds to the warning against 'Jezebel' in the following letter to Thyatira (Rev. 2:20–22); the Commons title of the file names Pergamon.

cur:objects-sinai-nativity-icon.summary: The Virgin reclines on a red mattress beside the manger where the swaddled Christ Child lies, watched by the ox and the ass, while angels hover above beneath the star. The Magi approach from the right, shepherds receive the angel's message, and below Joseph sits apart while the midwives bathe the Child. Painted in hot wax on a gold ground, the icon gathers the whole Christmas story around the newborn Lord.
facts: The encaustic technique — pigments suspended in hot wax — was used for the earliest Sinai icons before Iconoclasm and was largely abandoned later in favour of egg tempera (type).
cur:objects-sinai-nativity-icon.notes: Commons dates the icon to c. 6th century; this early dating could not be confirmed from a second source and a later (7th–8th century) date is possible. Image is small (382 px).
